newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ANALYSTS' COMMENTS ON POLYGRAM Q1 RESULTS (RPT).
newsitem.headline: ANALYSTS' COMMENTS ON POLYGRAM Q1 RESULTS (RPT).

text.p: Music and entertainment group PolyGram on Tuesday reported first-quarter net profits of 122 million guilders for 1997. Analysts had expected net profits of between 120 and 150 million, with consensus at 137 million.
Below is a collection of analysts' comments on the results.

"(The profit) is rather disappointing, though I've not seen the entire profit and loss account yet. I had expected it would be a bit up, due to the contribution of the music business, especially U2. We had Polygram as a sell. Looking at these figures, the first impression is that we'll keep it there."

"The results of the music division were OK, but film was disappointing. We expected (film) losses to widen, but they really plunged. The financial items were in line. There are some signs that things were improving towards the end of the first quarter and we expect this to continue in the second quarter. We have it as a hold and that will probably be maintained."

"The figure was slightly better than the 120 million guilders we expected, but in the lower range of market expectations, which explains the share price's reaction. At the presentation of its 1996 results, Polygram warned of flops in its film business, but apparently not everybody heard that. At first sight, these figures are no reason to change my hold recommendation or my estimate of 1997 earnings."

"On the basis of what we have till now, both the operating profits and the turnover are good. The bad perfomance of the film business was as expected, and music did well. It's too early too say if we'll change our forecast on this." -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
